name: Bajaj Finance Ltd
about: Bajaj Finance is mainly engaged in the business of lending. BFL has a diversified lending portfolio across retail, SME and commercial customers with a significant presence in urban and rural India. It also accepts public and corporate deposits and offers variety of financial services products to its customers.(Source : 202003 Annual Report Page No:124)

statements.text: Revenue compounded 25.2% a year over 5 years (FY21→FY26); profit after tax 34.3%.
Revenue growth accelerated from 16% to 23% YoY over the last 4 quarters.

cash.note: For lenders, operating cash flow mostly reflects loan-book growth; cash conversion isn't a meaningful test.

ledger.quote: I would say probably between 26%, 27% growth we should deliver now on a full year basis
ledger.statement: FY27 full-year growth of 26-27%
ledger.speaker: Rajeev Jain
ledger.evidence: Raised from 20-24% (G16) to 26-27% on the Q2 FY27 call. Management says H1 growth was 26% (C6), and AUM additions have run at INR38,000-39,000 crore a quarter for two quarters (C4). AUM is not in the facts. Revenue grew 22.8% YoY in Q2 FY27.

ledger.quote: the longer-term growth guidance of 23% to 25%
ledger.statement: Long-term growth of 23-25% (guidance unchanged)
ledger.speaker: Rajeev Jain
ledger.evidence: The long-term 23-25% guide is unchanged. The revenue proxy fits: 3y CAGR 25.6%, 5y 25.2%. AUM growth is not in the facts.

ledger.quote: we have to deliver the long-term 20% to 25% profit growth to investors in 19% to 21% return on equity
ledger.statement: Long-term PAT growth of 20-25% with return on equity of 19-21%
ledger.speaker: Rajeev Jain
ledger.evidence: The long-term guide is 20-25% PAT growth at 19-21% ROE. Reported ROE is 18.0% and the 3y PAT CAGR is 18.9%, both below their bands. Latest-quarter PAT growth was 28.7% YoY. Management instead cites 'core ROE of 19-20% on a 3-year basis' (C7), a different basis from reported ROE.
ledger.actual_text: ROE 18.0%; PAT CAGR 3y 18.9%; Q2 FY27 PAT +28.7% YoY

ledger.quote: In general, our guidance of 16% to 18%
ledger.statement: FY27 non-interest (fee) income growth of 16-18%
ledger.speaker: Rajeev Jain
ledger.evidence: Fee income growth of 16-18% for FY27. The facts contain no fee-income line and the year is half done.

ledger.quote: I had given a guidance of 10 to 15 basis point compression in the current year
ledger.statement: NIM compression of 10-15 bps in FY27, with a marginal additional headwind
ledger.speaker: Sandeep Jain
ledger.evidence: NIM compression of 10-15 bps, restated with a 'marginal additional headwind', so management itself now leans to or past the top of the range. The facts include no NIM. Revenue growth of 22.8% trails the 26-27% AUM growth guide.

ledger.quote: We remain pretty comfortable place to deliver a 25 to 40 basis point improvement in FY27 on opex-to-NTI
ledger.statement: Opex-to-NTI improvement of 25-40 bps in FY27
ledger.speaker: Rajeev Jain
ledger.evidence: Opex-to-NTI improvement of 25-40 bps, the third time this has been guided (G17, G8). The facts include no opex or NTI data.

ledger.quote: We are well on track to deliver between 60 million to 62 million new loans in FY27
ledger.statement: New loans of 60-62 million in FY27
ledger.speaker: Rajeev Jain
ledger.evidence: New loans of 60-62 million for FY27. Q2 FY27 delivered 13.5 million, or 4.5 million a month (C4). Q1 is not given. Hitting the target needs a seasonal H2 lift, which management attributes to a later festive season.

ledger.quote: Overall, we are confident of delivering 25 to 40 basis points improvement for FY '27 in opex to NTI.
ledger.statement: Opex to NTI to improve by 25-40 bps in FY27
ledger.speaker: Rajeev Jain
ledger.evidence: The Q1 FY27 opex-to-NTI guide of 25-40 bps was repeated unchanged on the Q2 FY27 call (G6). That rests only on management's word, since the facts cannot check it.

ledger.quote: By year-end we foresee 2,700 to 2,800 branches, all goes well, maybe 3,000 branches and AUM of between INR29,000 crores and INR31,000 crores, all organic.
ledger.statement: Gold loan AUM of INR29,000-31,000 crore and 2,700-2,800 branches by FY27 year-end
ledger.speaker: Rajeev Jain
ledger.evidence: Gold loan AUM of INR29,000-31,000 crore and 2,700-2,800 branches by FY27 end. No gold-loan AUM or branch count is in the inputs.

ledger.quote: this year the digital platform will deliver INR50,000 crores of business.
ledger.statement: Digital platform business of INR50,000 crore in FY27
ledger.speaker: Rajeev Jain
ledger.evidence: Digital platform business of INR50,000 crore in FY27. No digital-platform volume figure appears in the Q2 FY27 context.

ledger.quote: I am targeting that next year we should be delivering INR100,000 crores volume
ledger.statement: Digital platform volume of INR100,000 crore targeted for FY28
ledger.speaker: Rajeev Jain
ledger.evidence: Target of INR100,000 crore for FY28, and the period has not begun.

ledger.quote: that moderation 10 - 15 basis points is what we foresee at this juncture, give us a quarter.
ledger.statement: NIM moderation of 10-15 bps expected at this juncture
ledger.speaker: Rajeev Jain
ledger.evidence: In Q1 FY27 management guided 10-15 bps moderation and asked to 'give us a quarter'. The Q2 FY27 call kept the range but added a 'marginal additional headwind' (G5). NIM is not in the facts.

ledger.quote: The interesting thing is custom AI model, which is on track to go live in Q2.
ledger.statement: Custom AI model for B2B to go live in Q2FY27
ledger.speaker: Rajeev Jain
ledger.evidence: The custom B2B AI model was due live in Q2 FY27. That quarter has ended, and the Q2 FY27 passages (C5, C6) cover AI bots and agentic apps but never confirm the custom model launched.

ledger.quote: There are two new lines of business that we are at this juncture planning to launch by January, February.
ledger.statement: Two new lines of business to launch by Jan-Feb 2027
ledger.speaker: Rajeev Jain
ledger.evidence: Two new business lines are due by Jan-Feb 2027. The deadline has not arrived and the Q2 FY27 context has no update.

ledger.quote: we continue to be confident of adding 15 - 17 million new customers in FY27
ledger.statement: Add 15-17 million new customers in FY27
ledger.speaker: Rajeev Jain
ledger.evidence: Q2 FY27 added 4.42 million customers (C4), which annualises to about 17.7 million, at the top of the 15-17 million guide. Q1 additions are not given.

ledger.quote: we're confident of a 20% to 24% AUM growth
ledger.statement: FY27 AUM growth of 20-24%
ledger.speaker: Rajeev Jain
ledger.evidence: Drift: the guide was raised from 20-24% (Q4 FY26) to 26-27% (Q2 FY27, G1). Management says H1 ran at 26% (C6), above the original band.

ledger.quote: On opex to NTI, we expect to see continued improvement of 25 to 40 basis points from current levels.
ledger.statement: Opex to NTI to improve by 25-40 bps in FY27
ledger.speaker: Rajeev Jain
ledger.evidence: The 25-40 bps opex-to-NTI guide from Q4 FY26 was repeated in Q1 FY27 (G8) and Q2 FY27 (G6). The facts cannot check it.

ledger.quote: NIM, we expect marginal moderation.
ledger.statement: NIM expected to moderate marginally in FY27
ledger.speaker: Rajeev Jain

ledger.quote: We continue to guide for 4.4% to 4.6%.
ledger.statement: FY27 ROA guidance of 4.4-4.6%
ledger.speaker: Rajeev Jain
ledger.evidence: FY27 ROA guide of 4.4-4.6%, but the facts include no ROA. Reported ROE of 18.0% against a 19-20% guide points to softer returns, but does not settle the ROA guide.

ledger.quote: we continue to guide for 19% to 20%
ledger.statement: FY27 ROE guidance of 19-20%
ledger.speaker: Rajeev Jain
ledger.evidence: Latest reported ROE is 18.0%, 100 bps below the bottom of the 19-20% FY27 guide. Management now cites 'core ROE' on a 3-year basis (C7) and has flagged a capital raise (C7), which would dilute ROE further.

ledger.quote: we expect them to remain range bound and well within our long-term guidance
ledger.statement: GNPA and NNPA to remain range bound and within long-term guidance
ledger.speaker: Rajeev Jain

ledger.quote: We foresee gold loan portfolio to probably cross 5-odd percent of total AUM by FY'27.
ledger.statement: Gold loan portfolio to reach about 5% of AUM by FY27
ledger.speaker: Rajeev Jain
ledger.evidence: Gold loans to reach about 5% of AUM by FY27. The inputs give no gold-loan or total AUM split.

ledger.quote: We expect that it should come back to double-digit growth or the company growth momentum between Q2 and Q3 of FY'27.
ledger.statement: MSME growth to return to double-digit by Q2-Q3FY27
ledger.speaker: Rajeev Jain
ledger.evidence: The window is Q2-Q3 FY27, which runs to December 2026. The Q2 FY27 passages give no MSME growth figure.

ledger.quote: We are well on course to cross 5 million loans in a single month as a firm.
ledger.statement: Cross 5 million loans in a single month during FY27
ledger.speaker: Rajeev Jain
ledger.evidence: Target of 5 million loans in a single month. Q2 FY27 averaged 4.5 million a month (13.5 million per quarter, C4), and H2 has the festive season.
ledger.actual_text: Q2 FY27 average 4.5 million a month

ledger.quote: We orchestrate these 4 to deliver an outcome of 4.3% to 4.7% ROA
ledger.statement: Long-term ROA of 4.3-4.7%
ledger.speaker: Rajeev Jain
ledger.evidence: Long-term ROA of 4.3-4.7%, but no ROA is in the facts.

ledger.quote: 20% to 22% ROE to investors on a long-term basis
ledger.statement: Long-term ROE of 20-22%
ledger.speaker: Rajeev Jain

ledger.quote: we should be as a firm aspiring to grow 2x of what the system growth is
ledger.statement: Aspire to grow at 2x system growth, to be a top 5-6 lender in 5-7 years
ledger.speaker: Rajeev Jain
ledger.evidence: Aspiration to grow at 2x system growth over 5-7 years. The inputs give no system credit growth to compare against.

ledger.quote: the profit growth principally should be higher than balance sheet growth
ledger.statement: Profit growth to exceed balance sheet growth
ledger.speaker: Rajeev Jain

tones.label: mixed
tones.why: Management reiterates 23-25% long-term growth and 19-21% ROE and sets FY27 targets, but flags a possible RBI restriction under the draft regulation and a 10 bps rise in GNPA as uncertainties.

tones.label: confident
tones.why: Calls the quarter excellent and sets dated AI, digital and margin targets, while holding back on revising guidance until next quarter.

tones.label: confident
tones.why: Management says it is confident of 20-24% AUM growth and of ROA and ROE guidance, while stating the outlook is contingent on easing geopolitical tensions and macro stability.

context.speaker: Rajeev Jain
context.text: Consumer leverage remains a consumer-to-consumer play rather than a generic point. As you are aware, we continue to see consumer debt to GDP grow a little slower but continue to move forward. We are in public domain over the last three years that 3PL is a single univariate metric that continues to trouble us. We have brought that down from 14% to 7% in terms of origination my mandate to the team is to bring that down to 3.5% in the 6 months' time. That's really where we are principally headed. Despite, as I said, I'm looking at ultra-low credit metrics because we have seen that a customer who has multiple pieces of points of leverage that has a higher probability, tendency to flow into default. So, we will keep bringing down the 2PL, 3PL number business by business further. Further means by half or we'll half it by Feb again. So that's really what our proactive stance is it's bottoms-up customer- to-customer and leverage as a central dimension of our risk assessment process.

context.speaker: Sandeep Jain
context.text: Chintan, I think the right metric from a comparison perspective as you do compare between Q1, Q2, Q3 and Q4 is to look at Stage-2 and Stages-3 together, which has actually improved from 1.9% to 188 basis points, excluding gold loan. It's what we have also communicated in the presentation. The movement in the GNPA, it goes up in quarter two, mainly on account of number of days being higher in Q2 compared to Q1, which means that one additional month of GNPA flows in quarter one, quarter two always. And that has been the case always. If you look at past records also, that's how the numbers would show. This is mainly on a kind of number of days, nothing to do with portfolio quality or any kind of stress getting built up in the balance sheet.

context.speaker: Rajeev Jain
context.text: I will just make a point before, Is it to build resilience? The answer is yes. Okay? So, the fundamental reason for creating overlay, let me articulate it not because we see stress building. I want us to remember always that this is bullet proofing of the business. It is for resilience. We are a cyclical business. We will see credit costs go up marginally, credit costs go down marginally. It is for those marginal periods of when we go to two point, we went to a peak of from 1.75 to 2.15. Let me give you a cycle view of us as a firm. I mean that's a very low cycle view somebody could articulate argue that we go from 1.75% in a low period to historically. Now the number would reduce further, as I've said, to 2.15%. That's really, if you see last two has been. That's really a cyclicality for us as a firm. We would like to further strengthen that, I would say, narrow the band further so that we can in a cyclical business, reduce cyclicality is the and which is what we call resilience is the way thinking about the business model. And Sandeep, do you want to add something else?

These are fascinating numbers even for me, I would say. I didn't imagine we'll be growing quarterly between INR38,000 crores and INR39,000 crores on a run rate basis because that's been the case for the last two quarters now. I'll go back to panel 5, 6 and 7 to quickly give you highlights of the quarter. New loans grew 11% to 13.5 million. There is some level of noise in year-on-year number because last year's season was earlier this year’s season is later. We are well on track to deliver between 60 million to 62 million new loans in FY27. We added, as I said, 4.42 million new customers during the quarter.

We're getting a lot of learnings from these deployments. AI bots are now handling 75% of our DIY customer service volumes, disbursements, you can see the numbers, year-on-year 111%. So, as we deepen our understanding of enterprise AI and deploy it, we get experience, we get learnings. We're becoming more and more effective, both in terms of cost and in terms of experience of the customer and of the employee. Overall company has no 130-odd agents and 65 agentic applications. We are well on track to deliver 180-odd agentic applications and 600-odd agents for the year.

Overall, I would just say that the first half principally demonstrates the strength and scalability of our business model at this scale to grow 26% is I would say, good growth to be in while maintaining credit costs that, as I've said, that probably it's likely that in the 4 years, this is likely to be one of the lowest years on credit costs. We are well on track for that. And FINAI is moving rapidly from individual deployments to enterprise-wide transformation, both for employees and for consumers as we move forward. That's really from me.

So in absolute, the number may look large, but in terms of previous Page 14 of 19 Bajaj Finance Limited October 19, 2026 raise to balance sheet growth, and during this period, we have continued to deliver if you take core ROE of between 19% and 20% on a 3-year basis. So size or the quantum is actually smaller than what we raised last time around. We could very well raise part of this, you are right, from BHFL dilution. We have 3 years' time. That's point number one. And we are on track within that timeline. We have to do this.

So this would give BHFL some more time as well to transition their business model closer from super prime and prime to prime and near prime, and allow them to migrate their business, which would be eventually a lot more beneficial to BFL shareholders. Because at the end of the day, we intend to remain 75% holder, we today are 87% holder. So when we take a longer-term view and look at the transition that BHFL is undergoing at this point in time, we think we want to give them a little more time to repivot the business, which they are very well on track to. That's why I articulated that some of loans are now INR500-odd crores a month.

On disbursements, AI, voice and text bots did INR2,500 crores, we will do INR11,000 crores INR12,000 in the full year this year. On service, AI bots are now handling 71% of our DIY customer service volumes. 17 agentic applications have now got deployed out of 118, and we'll rapidly accelerate as we get into the year. I'm on panel 13. I'll just cover two odd points that it gives you texture on our data intelligence, consumer, agentic AI and custom AI models. The interesting thing is custom AI model, which is on track to go live in Q2. That should help us for our B2B business generate 0.5 million customers that we could not do earlier.

business.what_it_does: Retail-focused lender adding AUM at INR38,000-39,000 crore a quarter. In Q2 FY27 it booked 13.5 million new loans and added 4.42 million customers. Products include consumer loans, gold loans (through a branch network), MSME lending and a digital platform. It owns 87% of housing-finance subsidiary BHFL and intends to fall to a 75% holding. AI bots handle 75% of DIY service volumes. The inputs give no revenue split by segment.

segments.name: Consumer / retail lending
segments.comment: 13.5 million new loans in Q2 FY27 (+11% YoY), with 60-62 million guided for FY27. Origination share of 3+ loan (3PL) customers was cut from 14% to 7%, with a target of 3.5%.

segments.name: Gold loans
segments.comment: Targeted at INR29,000-31,000 crore of AUM, 2,700-2,800 branches and about 5% of total AUM by FY27 end.

segments.name: MSME
segments.comment: Guided back to double-digit growth between Q2 and Q3 FY27. The inputs give no figure.

segments.name: Housing finance (BHFL subsidiary)
segments.comment: 87% held, with a 75% holding intended. Repivoting from super-prime/prime towards prime/near-prime, with some loans now at about INR500 crore a month.

segments.name: Digital platform
segments.comment: Targeted at INR50,000 crore of business in FY27 and INR100,000 crore in FY28.

narrative_vs_numbers.claim: Growth is running ahead of plan, and the FY27 guide was raised from 20-24% to 26-27%.
narrative_vs_numbers.reality: Revenue YoY accelerated every quarter: 16.5%, 18.1%, 18.6%, then 22.8%. Q2 FY27 PAT rose 28.7% YoY. The direction matches, though revenue growth still trails the AUM guide by 3-4 points.

narrative_vs_numbers.claim: Management says it delivers 'core ROE of between 19% and 20% on a 3-year basis' and guides FY27 ROE at 19-20%.
narrative_vs_numbers.reality: Reported ROE is 18.0% and the 3y PAT CAGR is 18.9%, against a 20-25% long-term PAT-growth target. The 3y margin change is -600 bps. The 'core' framing covers a shortfall on reported numbers.

narrative_vs_numbers.claim: FY27 is likely one of the lowest credit-cost years in 4 years. The overlay is 'bullet proofing', not a response to stress, and the Q2 GNPA uptick is a day-count effect.
narrative_vs_numbers.reality: Q2 FY27 margin was 34.8%, against 33.1% a year earlier, consistent with lower credit costs. Stage 2+3 ex-gold improved only from 1.90% to 1.88%. The facts include no credit cost or GNPA, and Q3 FY26 margin dipped to 25.8% without explanation in the inputs.

bull.point: The FY27 growth guide was raised 6 points at the midpoint, from 20-24% to 26-27%. H1 grew 26% per management, AUM is adding INR38,000-39,000 crore a quarter, and revenue YoY has accelerated from 16.5% to 22.8% over four quarters.
Earnings are compounding: Q2 FY27 PAT rose 28.7% YoY and margin reached 34.8%, against 33.1% a year ago. TTM PAT is INR22,067 crore on INR90,330 crore of revenue.

Customer acquisition is at the top of guidance: 4.42 million added in Q2 FY27, which annualises to about 17.7 million against a 15-17 million guide. Risk is being tightened at the same time, with 3PL origination share halved from 14% to 7% and a 3.5% target within 6 months.

bear.point: Returns are below guide: reported ROE is 18.0% against 19-20% for FY27 and 19-21% long-term. Management is shifting to a 3-year 'core ROE' basis and flags a capital raise. D/E is 4.08x on INR5.02 lakh crore of borrowings.

Spreads are thinning: the 10-15 bps NIM-compression guide now carries a 'marginal additional headwind', and Q2 FY27 revenue growth of 22.8% runs below the 26-27% balance-sheet growth guide. The 3y PAT CAGR of 18.9% sits below the 20-25% target.

Growth is being pushed while risk controls tighten: the growth guide went up even as management builds overlays, plans to halve 3PL origination again by February, and sees GNPA rising in Q2. The 25.8% margin in Q3 FY26 shows how much one bad quarter can cost.

questions: Reported ROE is 18.0% against your 19-20% FY27 guide. What reported (not 'core') ROE do you expect for FY27, and how many basis points will the planned capital raise take off it?
How many basis points beyond the 10-15 bps range is the 'marginal additional headwind' on NIM, and is it funding cost, mix, or pricing to support 26-27% growth?

Q2 FY27 delivered 13.5 million new loans, or 4.5 million a month. What H2 run-rate does the 60-62 million FY27 guide require, and how much volume does halving 3PL origination again by February remove?
